evidence: This is a direct report of experimental observations with reference to figure.

claim: At P12, dense plexus were observed, with fibers displaying numerous branching points and each fiber containing fine extensions and protrusions, similar to what was seen in older animals and adults.
source: At this age, we observed dense plexus, with fibers displaying numerous branching points and each fiber containing fine extensions and protrusions, similar to what was seen in older animals and adults (Figure 8G).
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental observations with reference to figure.

claim: The number of RSC fibers in PHR increase gradually from single fibers at P1 to adult-like densities around P12.
source: Based on these observations we concluded that the number of RSC fibers in PHR increase gradually from single fibers at P1 to adult-like densities around P12.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental observations over developmental time.

claim: In some anterograde tracing experiments (n=44), a few retrogradely labeled neurons were observed within the dorsal half of subiculum (SUB).
source: In some (n=44), we observed a few retrogradely labeled neurons within the dorsal half of subiculum (SUB).
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental observations.

claim: After fast blue injections in PHR of pups, labeled neurons were identified in RSC in superficial layer V at P5 and P11.
source: After fast blue injections in PHR of pups we identified labeled neurons in RSC in superficial layer V at P5 (Figure 9A) and P11 (Figure 9B)
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental observations with reference to figures.

claim: The RSC-PHR projections are adult-like with respect to the layer in which the neurons are located already during the first postnatal week of development.
source: which suggested that the RSC-PHR projections are adult-like with respect to the layer in which the neurons are located already during the first postnatal week of development.
evidence: This is an inference based on retrograde tracing observations.

claim: All injections that did not cover parts of layer V (n=8) did not result in any labeled axons in PHR.
source: These observations are in line with our anterograde material in which we observed that all injections that did not cover parts of layer V (n=8) did not result in any labeled axons in PHR.
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental observations.

claim: The postnatal RSC projects densely to all layers of PrS and posterior POR and deep layers of PaS and MEC and weakly to deep layers of LEC and to SUB.
source: We conclude that the postnatal RSC projects densely to all layers of PrS and posterior POR and deep layers of PaS and MEC and weakly to deep layers of LEC and to SUB.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on experimental observations.

claim: The origin of RSC-PHR projections are neurons located in superficial parts of layer V of RSC.
source: Our retrograde experiments showed that the origin of these projections were neurons located in superficial parts of layer V of RSC.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on retrograde tracing experiments.

claim: These findings are in accordance with previous work in the adult.
source: These findings are in accordance with previous work in the adult (Wyss and Van Groen, 1992; Shibata, 1994; Burwell and Amaral, 1998a; Jones and Witter, 2007).
evidence: This statement compares current findings with prior literature.

claim: The RSC projections to PrS, PaS and EC are topographically organized similarly already in the youngest postnatal rats and in adult rats.
source: Additionally, we report that the RSC projections to PrS, PaS and EC are topographically organized similarly already in the youngest postnatal rats and in adult rats (Figure 10).
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study based on experimental data with reference to figure.

claim: Rostral RSC only projects to dorsal PHR, while caudal RSC projects to additional more ventral parts of PHR.
source: The notion that rostral RSC only projects to dorsal PHR, while caudal RSC projects to additional more ventral parts of PHR is in accordance with previous work in the adult (Wyss and Van Groen, 1992; Shibata, 1994; Jones and Witter, 2007).
evidence: This is a finding that is consistent with prior literature.

claim: Dorsal RSC (A30) projects preferentially to distal PrS, PaS and medial MEC.
source: Second, dorsal RSC (A30) projects preferentially to distal PrS, PaS and medial MEC
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: More ventral parts of RSC (A29) project significantly more to proximal PrS and more lateral parts of MEC.
source: while more ventral parts of RSC (A29) project significantly more to proximal PrS and more lateral parts of MEC.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: The topographies of A30 projecting to distal PrS/medial MEC and A29 projecting to proximal PrS/lateral MEC have not been reported in earlier studies.
source: To our knowledge, such topographies have not been reported in earlier studies.
evidence: This statement identifies a novel finding of the study.

claim: A30 is preferentially connected to distal PrS, PaS and medial MEC, while A29 is preferentially connected to proximal PrS and more lateral parts of MEC, but not PaS.
source: The observation that A30 is preferentially connected to distal PrS, PaS and medial MEC, while A29 is preferentially connected to proximal PrS and more lateral parts of MEC, but not PaS is in line with other connectional and functional differences.
evidence: This is a summary of findings that is consistent with other known differences.

claim: The PrS to MEC projection is topographically organized such that distal PrS projects to medial MEC, while proximal PrS projects to more lateral parts of MEC.
source: The PrS to MEC projection is topographically organized such that distal PrS projects to medial MEC, while proximal PrS projects to more lateral parts of MEC (Shipley, 1975; Honda and Ishizuka, 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Distal SUB projects to distal PrS and medial MEC, while more proximal parts of SUB project to proximal PrS and more lateral MEC.
source: Furthermore, these partner domains in PrS and MEC are selectively innervated by different areas of SUB along its transverse axis such that distal SUB projects to distal PrS and medial MEC, while more proximal parts of SUB, with the exclusion of the very proximal part, project to proximal PrS and more lateral MEC (Witter, 2006; O'Reilly et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: There exists a connectional route linking A30, medial MEC, distal SUB and distal PrS to each other.
source: This indicates the existence of a connectional route linking A30, medial MEC, distal SUB and distal PrS to each other.
evidence: This is an inference based on the connectivity patterns described.

claim: A parallel route links A29 with more lateral MEC, more proximal SUB and proximal PrS.
source: A parallel route links A29 with more lateral MEC, more proximal SUB and proximal PrS.
evidence: This is an inference based on the connectivity patterns described.

claim: Electrophysiological properties of neurons in MEC show a transverse gradient, indicative that more medially positioned grid cells might be more precisely spatially tuned.
source: Although no clear transverse gradients in spatial modulation have been reported in MEC, electrophysiological properties of neurons show a transverse gradient, indicative that more medially positioned grid cells might be more precisely spatially tuned (Canto and Witter, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Neurons in distal SUB are more spatially modulated compared to those in proximal SUB.
source: Furthermore, neurons in distal SUB are more spatially modulated compared to those in proximal SUB (Sharp and Green, 1994).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: A30 is connected preferentially to more spatially modulated neurons in medial MEC and distal SUB compared to A29 which is more connected to neurons in lateral MEC and more proximal SUB.
source: All observations thus point to a differentiation of A29 and A30 where A30 is connected preferentially to more spatially modulated neurons in medial MEC and distal SUB compared to A29 which is more connected to neurons in lateral MEC and more proximal SUB.
evidence: This is an inference based on the connectivity patterns and functional properties described.

claim: The projections to anterior cingulate cortex are differentially organized for A29 and A30.
source: The projections to anterior cingulate cortex are differentially organized for A29 and A30
evidence: This statement is based on known anatomical differences.

claim: A30 is connected to visual area A17 and A18b, while A29 is only connected to A18b.
source: and while A30 is connected to visual area A17 and A18b, A29 is only connected to A18b.
evidence: This statement is based on known anatomical differences.

claim: A29 is connected to the anterodorsal and anteroventral thalamic nuclei while A30 preferentially connects with the anteromedial nucleus.
source: With respect to thalamic connections, A29 is connected to the anterodorsal and anteroventral nuclei while A30 preferentially connects with the anteromedial nucleus (van Groen and Wyss, 1990, 1992; Shibata, 1998; van Groen and Wyss, 2003; Jones et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: These connectional differences are in line with reported functional differences between A29 and A30.
source: Taken together, these connectional differences are in line with reported functional differences between the two areas (van Groen et al., 2004; Vann and Aggleton, 2005; Pothuizen et al., 2009; Pothuizen et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Functional differentiation between A29 and A30 could possibly result in functional differences along the transverse axes of PrS, PaS and MEC.
source: Such a functional differentiation between A29 and A30 could thus possibly result in functional differences along the transverse axes of PrS, PaS and MEC.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the connectivity patterns described.

claim: During the postnatal period there was an overall increase in the density of labeled axonal branches in all PHR subregions.
source: During the postnatal period we observed an overall increase in the density of labeled axonal branches in all PHR subregions.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental observations over developmental time.

claim: The time window of increased density of RSC afferents in PHR is paralleled by several anatomical and physiological changes in PHR.
source: Interestingly, the time window of increased density of RSC afferents in PHR is paralleled by several anatomical and physiological changes in PHR.
evidence: This is an observation that relates the current findings to other known developmental changes.

claim: EC afferents originating in PaS and PrS become functional from P8 and mature gradually until they are fully adult-like around P14.
source: EC afferents originating in PaS and PrS become functional from P8 and mature gradually until they are fully adult-like around P14 (Canto et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Similar developmental timescales have been reported for the functional development of intralaminar projections within EC.
source: Similar developmental timescales have also been reported for the functional development of intralaminar projections within EC (O'Reilly et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: RSC axons destined for PHR migrate directly into their area of termination and thereafter keeps their position constant while the number of axonal branches and the total axonal spread increases gradually until they reach adult-like plexus features.
source: Our temporal analysis revealed that RSC axons destined for PHR migrate directly into their area of termination and thereafter keeps their position constant while the number of axonal branches and the total axonal spread increases gradually until they reach adult-like plexus features.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on developmental analysis of experimental data.

claim: Projections originating in different parts of RSC show a striking terminal topography already during the first postnatal week.
source: This observation is supported by our center of mass analyses of the early perinatal RSC to PHR projections, showing that projections originating in different parts of RSC show a striking terminal topography already during the first postnatal week.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: The topographical organization of RSC terminals in PHR is present before spatially modulated neurons are present in PHR.
source: Even though no published experiments have investigated whether border cells and head-direction cells are present before the second postnatal week, our data indicate that the topographical organization of RSC terminals in PHR is present before spatially modulated neurons are present in PHR
evidence: This is an inference based on the developmental timeline of RSC projections compared to the known timeline of spatial cell emergence.

claim: Adult-like axonal densities of RSC projections can be observed approximately at the same time-point as the first border cells and head-direction cells are observed in PHR.
source: and that adult-like axonal densities can be observed approximately at the same time-point as the first border cells and head-direction cells are observed in PHR.
evidence: This is an inference based on the developmental timeline of RSC projections compared to the known timeline of spatial cell emergence.

claim: This conclusion is comparable to what has been observed for intrinsic HF-PHR connectivity which is also topographically organized already at early postnatal periods.
source: This conclusion is comparable to what has been observed for intrinsic HF-PHR connectivity which is also topographically organized already at early postnatal periods, demonstrating increased plexus densities for intrinsic HF-PHR projections during ongoing development (Fricke and Cowan, 1977; Borrell et al., 1999; O'Reilly et al., 2013; O'Reilly et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement compares current findings with prior literature on other developing projections.

claim: For thalamocortical projections in the visual system of monkeys, cats and ferrets, the first arriving axons in the visual cortex already show a topographical organization into ocular dominance columns.
source: For instance, for thalamocortical projections in the visual system of both monkeys, cats and ferrets, the first arriving axons in the visual cortex already show a topographical organization into ocular dominance columns (Horton and Hocking, 1996; Crowley and Katz, 2000; Crair et al., 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research in other systems.

claim: In the rat ventral posterior thalamic nucleus, projections to the somatosensory cortex show that the first arriving axons target distinct areas later forming a defined barrel.
source: Similarly, the rat ventral posterior thalamic nucleus issue projections to the somatosensory cortex in which the first arriving axons target distinct areas later forming a defined barrel (Catalano et al., 1996).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research in another system.

claim: Sensory inputs to the olfactory bulb are present long before neurons display a receptive field.
source: Sensory inputs to the olfactory bulb are present long before neurons display a receptive field.
evidence: This statement is based on prior research in another system.

claim: The development of inputs to the olfactory bulb is independent of activity in sensory receptors, which suggests that the development of topographies in the olfactory bulb is experience independent.
source: Moreover, the development of these inputs is independent of activity in sensory receptors, which suggests that the development of topographies in the olfactory bulb is experience independent (Lin et al., 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The development of projections from RSC to PHR is experience independent.
source: The same conclusion apparently holds for the projections from RSC to PHR
evidence: This is an inference based on the similarity to other developing systems.

claim: In the retinogeniculate projection in several species, there is an overshoot of axonal terminals, which are initially diffuse and later pruned into an adult-like topography.
source: These findings are different from what has been reported for the retinogeniculate projection in several species. In this projection, there is an overshoot of axonal terminals, which are initially diffuse and later pruned into an adult-like topography (Rakic, 1976; Linden et al., 1981; Shatz, 1983; Godement et al., 1984).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research in another system.

claim: Distinct molecular- or activity based principles might govern the axonal termination patterns in different neural projections.
source: These differences might imply that distinct molecular- or activity based principles governs the axonal termination patterns in different neural projections.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the differences observed between different developing systems.

claim: The topographical organization of PHR connectivity is present when the first RSC axons arrive in PHR.
source: The results presented in this study thus lead us to conclude that the topographical organization of PHR connectivity is present when the first RSC axons arrive in PHR.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study based on experimental data.

claim: The densities of the terminal plexus appear to develop gradually without any clear signs of pruning.
source: The densities of the terminal plexus appear to develop gradually without any clear signs of pruning, though it remains to be determined whether connectional reorganization occurs at the synaptic level during development.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental observations, with acknowledgment of limitations.

claim: The first plexus with adult-like densities can be observed around P12 which is around the time when the first spatially modulated neurons in PHR have been observed (P11).
source: The first plexus with adult-like densities can be observed around P12 which is around the time when the first spatially modulated neurons in PHR have been observed (P11)
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data and comparison with prior literature.

claim: The first adult-like RSC plexus in PHR appears before eye-opening and before the animals start to navigate (around P15).
source: but before eye-opening and before the animals starts to navigate (around P15)
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data and known developmental milestones.

claim: The first adult-like RSC plexus in PHR appears before adult like grid cells are observed in PHR (after P25).
source: and thus before adult like grid cells are observed in PHR (after P25; Langston et al., 2010; Wills et al., 2010; Bjerknes et al., 2014; Bjerknes et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data and comparison with prior literature.

claim: RSC afferents might be important for the development of head-direction and border cells.
source: These findings suggest that RSC afferents might be important for the development of head-direction and border cells.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the temporal relationship between RSC projection development and spatial cell emergence.
